name: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
problem: FlashAttention reached only 25-40% of peak FLOP/s because its work partitioning across thread blocks and warps caused low occupancy and redundant shared-memory traffic.
mechanism: Same IO-aware exact algorithm, different schedule. Three changes: (1) additionally parallelise the non-matmul FLOPs (the softmax rescaling) across thread blocks, not just the matmuls, so fewer of them are serialised; (2) parallelise the attention computation ACROSS thread blocks even for a single query head, raising occupancy; (3) within a thread block, distribute work between warps to cut shared-memory read/write traffic. Ships as a CUDA extension with a separate backward kernel.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): ~2x speedup vs FlashAttention, reaching 50-73% of theoretical maximum FLOP/s on A100 and getting close to GEMM efficiency; end-to-end GPT-style training at up to 225 TFLOPs/s per A100 (72% model FLOPs utilisation). Baseline is FlashAttention v1, not a naive implementation.
